title: US Gaming Market Dips for First Time in a Year as UFC 6 Tops June Charts
excerpt: Circana's June data shows EA Sports UFC 6 debuting at number one, Star Fox cracking the top five, and Xbox console sales surging 86 percent — but overall spending declined for the first time since mid-2025.
body:
The United States video game market recorded a spending decline in June 2026 for the first time in twelve months, according to data released by market research firm Circana. The downturn arrives despite strong individual performances from several titles and a notable surge in Xbox hardware sales.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=T2MP_T2e-aU

UFC 6 Lands the Top Spot

EA Sports UFC 6, which launched on June 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, debuted at number one on Circana's monthly sales chart. The mixed martial arts title — priced at $69.99 for the standard edition — entered a relatively quiet release window and capitalised on the gap between major launches.

The Nintendo Switch 2 continued its dominance as the best-selling console platform in the US for the month, maintaining momentum from its June 2025 launch. The console has now sold approximately 5.9 million units in its first twelve months on the American market, making it the second-fastest-selling Nintendo console in US history behind only the Game Boy Advance, which reached 6.5 million in its first year.

Star Fox Cracks the Top Five

Nintendo's Star Fox remake, released on June 25 for the Switch 2, entered the monthly chart in the top five despite having only six days of tracked sales in the reporting period. The game debuted at number one on both the UK physical charts and Japan's Switch 2 digital charts, with UK first-week physical sales of approximately 11,800 units — nearly double what Star Fox Zero managed at launch in 2016.

In Japan, Famitsu data showed Star Fox selling 41,680 copies in its opening week, topping the software chart. The title is also currently the number one best-seller on Amazon US for video games.

Xbox Surges, Physical Sales Crater

In a surprising development, Xbox Series X|S console dollar sales jumped 86% in June compared to the prior month. The spike appears driven by a combination of factors: a Walmart promotion and consumers rushing to purchase consoles ahead of a price increase taking effect August 1. The launch of GTA 6 pre-orders on June 25 may have also contributed to hardware movement across platforms.

Meanwhile, the state of physical game sales continued its alarming decline. According to Circana's Mat Piscatella, only seven PS5 games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies in the entire year to date. In the most recent tracked week, just two PS5 titles managed more than 10,000 physical units. Sony has already announced it will cease production of PlayStation discs from January 2028.

The Bigger Picture

Year-to-date, the top-selling games in the US remain Resident Evil Requiem (approximately 7 million copies), Crimson Desert (6 million), MLB The Show 26, 007 First Light (3 million), and Forza Horizon 6 — all of which launched in the first five months of the year. Total video game spending through May was up 4% year-over-year at approximately $23 billion, but June's decline suggests the market may be entering a softer patch ahead of the holiday season.

The average price of a new console has climbed to $502, up 14% from the prior year, a figure that reflects both the Switch 2's $449 launch price and Xbox's price increases. Whether the November 19 launch of GTA 6 — the most anticipated release in gaming history — will reignite spending growth remains the industry's central question for the second half of 2026.
